channel_name: The Prof G Show · Scott Galloway
video_title: “I Lost 94% on This Stock. AI Valuations Are Next.”
gist: Prof G Office Hours Q&A: Galloway concedes a ~94% loss on his Vertical Aerospace PIPE (now ~40 cents, under strategic review) while staying bullish on eVTOL, and likens it to AI where he expects valuations to collapse but the technology to endure like railroads. He also cites data that AI is creating more jobs than it destroys, calls Nike at ~$35 an attractive fallen-angel pick, and preaches capping single positions at 3-4% of net worth; the back half covers non-market parenting and friendship questions.

themes.theme: Vertical Aerospace post-mortem and eVTOL outlook

insights.claim: Scott Galloway's $4.5M PIPE investment in Vertical Aerospace (May 2025, ~$5/share) is down ~94%, with the stock now around 40 cents.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: Illustrates how capital-starved eVTOL challengers can be wiped out even with a well-known backer; size eVTOL bets accordingly.
insights.quote: The stock was hovering at around $5 a share at the time. Today, it's around 40 cents.

insights.claim: Vertical Aerospace has launched a strategic review with Jefferies as financial advisor, and Galloway expects a possible sale or pre-packaged bankruptcy in which debt holders recover value and equity may be reissued.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: A strategic review at a sub-$1 stock often signals sale/restructuring where equity gets wiped; debt/notes are the better-protected layer.
insights.quote: If they sell the company, it might be a pre-packaged bankruptcy where they declare bankruptcy and then the debt holders get some money back

insights.claim: Despite the equity collapse, Vertical Aerospace has made operational progress: second company to complete a piloted transition flight in a full-scale tilt-rotor eVTOL (2026), ~$100M new financing this year, ex-Airbus executive Fabrice Brégier as chair, and a 60,000 sq ft Bristol assembly center targeting certification in 2029.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: Technical milestones are not rescuing equity value; in capital-intensive aviation, funding runway dominates technical progress for stock outcomes.

insights.claim: Archer won a competitive bid to be the official air taxi provider of the LA28 Olympic Games, using its Midnight aircraft for VIPs, fans and emergency services.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: A visible high-profile deployment milestone for the better-capitalized US eVTOL leader; watch as a commercialization catalyst.

insights.claim: Galloway refuses to recommend any stock trading at ~40 cents because the price signals the market expects bankruptcy, making buying it pure speculation where creditors, not equity, get paid.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: Avoid averaging down into distressed equities priced for bankruptcy; consider the capital structure first.
insights.quote: Penny stocks are penny stocks for a reason and basically this is kind of just pure speculation at this point.

insights.claim: Aviation is a notorious capital sinkhole — like renovating a house times ten, with doubled budgets and timelines — and the eVTOL industry is in a capital war where the least-funded players trade at a small fraction of competitors' values.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: In eVTOL, back the best-capitalized players; cash position is the key differentiator.
insights.quote: It's like renovating a house times 10, double the budget, double the timeline.

insights.claim: Galloway remains bullish on eVTOL as the 'last mile' of travel, arguing airport-to-home ground transit can take as long as the flight itself, which makes it the next frontier.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: Long-term demand case for urban air mobility is intact even as early equity holders get wiped out.
insights.quote: the last mile is definitely something's going to happen there. That is the next, I think the final frontier.

insights.claim: Galloway missed a later Vertical Aerospace PIPE at about $2/share, which has since fallen ~80%, and did not participate in a Boom Technologies cram-down round — after which Boom found one of its engines useful as a data-center power source and is reportedly raising at ~10x that valuation.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: AI data-center power demand can re-rate unrelated hardware companies; pivots into energy for data centers are a recurring value catalyst.
insights.quote: they found that one of their engines would be a great source of energy for data centers, and now I think the company's raising money at 10 times that valuation

insights.claim: Galloway admits his aviation investments may have been clouded by his personal passion for aviation and that he 'doubled down on the wrong companies'.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: A reminder to discount investor enthusiasm for sectors they personally love.
insights.quote: So I've doubled down on the wrong companies and not participated in the right companies.

themes.theme: AI valuations vs. AI technology (railroad analogy)

insights.claim: Galloway believes current AI valuations will not survive, but the technology itself will prove seminal and transformative — the same pattern as railroads, where early investors were carried out on stretchers.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: Separate the technology thesis from valuation; expect a drawdown/bankruptcies in AI equities even if adoption continues — favor pick-and-shovel or later-entry positions.
insights.quote: I don't think these valuations are going to survive in the AI market, but I think the technology will survive

insights.claim: Galloway applies the same 'transformative technology, value-destroying for early investors' framework to eVTOLs: bankruptcies along the way, but the technology survives.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: For frontier tech, early equity often transfers value to later entrants and creditors; time entries after the shakeout.
insights.quote: The railroads were transformative technology, but investors got taken out on stretchers, at least the early investors.

insights.claim: Galloway caps any single stock at 3–4% of total net worth, so even a ~94% loss carries little emotional or financial damage — diversification is 'Kevlar'.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: Hard position-size caps let you take venture-like bets without catastrophic downside.
insights.quote: I never put now more than three or 4% of my total net worth into anyone stock.

insights.claim: Concentration is appropriate early in a career (e.g., in your own company), but once you have an asset base you should diversify; most very wealthy people were concentrated in their own company when young.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: Shift from concentration to diversification as wealth accumulates.
insights.quote: The moment you have an asset base, the moment you have some wealth, you want to diversify.

insights.claim: Citing The Economist, Galloway says AI has created about 1 million American jobs versus roughly 200,000 AI-attributed layoffs since mid-2023, including electricians, HVAC specialists and grid engineers building data centers.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: Data-center buildout is a labor-demand engine; skilled trades and grid/electrical contractors are beneficiaries.
insights.quote: The Economist estimates AI has created about 1 million American jobs versus roughly 200,000 layoffs attributed to AI since mid 2023.

insights.claim: Data-center maintenance jobs advertise pay roughly 40% above similar work elsewhere, signaling a tight labor market around AI infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: Labor cost inflation is a rising input cost for data-center builders/operators and a tailwind for trade-labor providers.

insights.claim: Predicted AI-driven obsolescence has not materialized in some fields: radiology residency programs offered a record 1,208 positions with pay as high as ~$571K, and paralegal employment rose 11% vs ~2% for the overall economy.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: Beware consensus narratives about wholesale job replacement; jobs are bundles of tasks and augmentation often raises demand.
insights.quote: Jeffrey Hinton, considered the godfather of AI, said we should stop training radiologists.

insights.claim: Jobs built around one or two tasks are most exposed to AI: since January 2023, employment fell about 10% among customer service workers and about 15% among secretaries/administrative assistants, and long-haul trucking is highly exposed.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: Watch BPO/call-center, admin staffing and trucking labor models for disruption; companies with heavy such headcount may see margin gains.
insights.quote: Jobs built around one or two tasks like long haul trucking are the most exposed.

insights.claim: Citing Noah Smith, Galloway argues that if total AI is limited by compute and energy, humans retain good jobs even if AI beats them at every task (comparative advantage), and that the '80% of workers have 10% of tasks affected' stat measures involvement, not automation.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: Compute and energy scarcity constrain AI substitution; supports compute/energy as the bottleneck investments.

insights.claim: Galloway argues AI productivity gains, like past gains, will be captured by shareholders unless legislation redirects flows of capital toward earners and consumers.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: Policy risk: potential redistribution legislation targeting AI-driven profits.

insights.claim: Over time AI will push workers toward roles where 'the human is the product' — nurses, therapists, teachers, trainers, chefs, performers, caregivers — categories already employing nearly 50 million Americans.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: Human-centric services (care, education, experiences) are relatively AI-resilient labor pools.

insights.claim: Nike has fallen from a pandemic high of ~$177 to ~$35/share (~80% off), with fiscal 2027 Q1 revenue around $11B vs $11.7B a year earlier, China sales down 30% since 2021, and removal from the S&P 100 after 18 years.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: Quantifies the depth of Nike's derating and revenue stagnation for anyone evaluating a turnaround.
insights.quote: it reached a high of $177 during the pandemic and [clears throat] today, get this, it's at $35 a share.

insights.claim: Nike's biggest problem is its retail relationships: the pandemic-era direct-to-consumer push under John Donahoe lifted margins but alienated retail partners who drove much of its demand and left a stale product lineup, letting Hoka and On Running take share.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: DTC pivots can hollow out wholesale demand; Hoka/On are the share-takers; Nike's wholesale repair will take years.
insights.quote: the new brands, Hoka or On Running came in and just ate their lunch

insights.claim: Western consumer brands (Nike, Estee Lauder, Starbucks, North Face, Tesla, Mercedes, luxury) get progressively squeezed in China as it learns from high-IP imports and backs local low-cost competitors.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: Discount China growth for Western consumer brands; local champions erode share over time.
insights.quote: slowly but surely the western brand begins to become asphyxiated

insights.claim: Galloway thinks Nike at ~$35 is 'probably a really good stock pick' — an injured but not career-ending brand with distribution, human capital, global resonance, a culture-savvy CEO in Elliot Hill, and room for cost cutting.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: Contrarian long candidate; watch wholesale relationship repair, product refresh, and cost cuts as catalysts.
insights.quote: Brands Brands typically they get injured, but they very rarely die.

insights.claim: Galloway is screening 'fallen angels' such as Netflix and Nike, noting Moderna already recovered after he looked at it, and admits his weakness is waiting for things to get cheaper.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: Signals a contrarian value watchlist of beaten-down quality names.
insights.quote: I'm looking at Netflix, I'm looking at Nike, I'm looking at a lot of fallen angels.
